gloss: Murasaki Shikibu (author of The Tale of Genji)

definitions.gloss: Murasaki Shikibu, Heian court lady and author of The Tale of Genji
definitions.explanation: The writer, active around the year 1000, who served at the imperial court and wrote {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}, often called the world's first novel. She also left a diary of court life.

examples.japanese: {紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}は{平安時代|へいあんじだい}の{作家|さっか}だ。
examples.english: Murasaki Shikibu was a writer of the Heian period.

examples.japanese: {源氏物語|げんじものがたり}は{紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}によって{書|か}かれた。
examples.english: The Tale of Genji was written by Murasaki Shikibu.

examples.japanese: {紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}が{宮中|きゅうちゅう}で{見|み}た{人々|ひとびと}の{様子|ようす}は、{日記|にっき}にも{細|こま}かく{記|しる}されている。
examples.english: What Murasaki Shikibu saw of the people at court is also recorded in detail in her diary.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}の{源氏物語|げんじものがたり}: Murasaki Shikibu's Tale of Genji
- {紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}{日記|にっき}: The Diary of Lady Murasaki
- {清少納言|せいしょうなごん}と{紫式部|むらさきしきぶ}: Sei Shonagon and Murasaki Shikibu, the paired names of Heian women's writing

CULTURAL NOTE:
Every Japanese student meets her in school, so the name stands for classical literature and for female authorship generally. Neither {紫|むらさき} nor {式部|しきぶ} is a real personal name: {式部|しきぶ} refers to her father's court post and {紫|むらさき} to a character in her own novel.

The same word also names a shrub, {紫式部|むらさきしきぶ} (Japanese beautyberry), whose purple berries were felt to suit her.
